about.label: About the park
about.heading: An urban oasis by the Mekong
about.lead: Located in the center of Vientiane, Chao Anouvong Park stretches along the Mekong River and is one of the city's most popular public spaces.
about.paragraph1: The park is named after King Anouvong, a famous figure in Lao history. His bronze statue stands tall, holding a sword in one hand and pointing towards Thailand across the Mekong with the other, symbolizing the independence and dignity of the Lao people.
about.paragraph2: During the day, it is a lush green promenade; in the evening, as the Mekong sunset turns the sky golden, the park transforms into a vibrant night market and a hub for citizen recreation.
about.quote: Here you can see the most authentic street life of Vientiane and the most beautiful sunset.

highlights.title: King Anouvong Statue
highlights.desc: The majestic bronze statue of King Anouvong is one of Vientiane's iconic landmarks.

highlights.title: Mekong Sunset
highlights.desc: Stroll along the riverside path and watch the sunset glow over the wide Mekong River.

highlights.title: Vientiane Night Market
highlights.desc: As night falls, the red-roofed tents next to the park connect into the largest night market in Vientiane.

editorTip.text: Arrive around 17:30 to watch the sunset, then explore the night market for street food.

eco.label: Riverbank & nature
eco.heading: Feel the breath of the Mekong
eco.quote: A mother river flowing endlessly — witnessing the city's sunsets and dawns.
eco.intro: Built along the Mekong River, Chao Anouvong Park is not only the city's flood embankment, but also a green space for citizens to get close to nature. The morning breeze and evening coolness make it an ideal place to escape the tropical heat.

micro.title: Cool evenings
micro.desc: The river breeze after sunset is perfect for walking or jogging.

micro.title: Wide riverbanks
micro.desc: In the dry season, large sandbars emerge; in the wet season, the river is full.

micro.title: Shaded by trees
micro.desc: The park is planted with tropical trees, providing shade during the day.

plants.title: Frangipani (Plumeria)
plants.desc: The national flower of Laos (Dok Champa), seen everywhere in the park.

plants.title: Tropical palms & lawns
plants.desc: Well-maintained green spaces, perfect for family picnics.

history.label: History & Culture
history.heading: The Gaze of King Anouvong
history.intro: The park's name and its central statue carry the deep memories of the Lao people's independence and dignity.

blocks.title: Who was Chao Anouvong?
blocks.text: Chao Anouvong (1767–1829) was the last king of the Kingdom of Vientiane. In the early 19th century, he attempted to rebel against Siamese (Thai) rule and fight for Lao independence. Although he ultimately failed, he is regarded as a national hero by the Lao people.

blocks.title: Symbolism of the statue
blocks.text: In the center of the park, the King's bronze statue stands 8 meters tall (14 meters with the base). Wearing a battle cloak, holding a sword in one hand, and pointing firmly towards Thailand across the river with the other, it symbolizes the determination to defend the territory.

blocks.title: Background of the park
blocks.text: The park was inaugurated in 2010 to commemorate the 450th anniversary of the founding of Vientiane. It not only beautified the Mekong riverbank but also became an important venue for national celebrations and holiday gatherings.

blocks.title: The riverbank today
blocks.text: The smoke of history has long dissipated, and today Chao Anouvong Park is a symbol of peace and prosperity. People walk, exercise, and enjoy food here, perfectly blending the weight of history with modern tranquility.

legend.title: Memory of a National Hero
legend.text: In the Lao historical narrative, Chao Anouvong is synonymous with courage. Locals often offer flowers and incense in front of the statue to express their reverence and remembrance for the King.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: This statue is one of the largest bronze statues in Laos. During specific festivals, grand ceremonies and commemorative events are held here, and the King's statue is surrounded by flowers.

folklore.title: Riverside Life
folklore.tale: For the citizens of Vientiane, the Mekong River is not only a natural boundary but also the center of life. The night river breeze takes away the heat of the day, and people gather here, continuing the riverside lifestyle passed down for generations.
folklore.shrine: Please maintain proper respect near the King's statue. Do not make inappropriate gestures or climb the base.

concrete.title: Modern landscape & history
concrete.text: The park's design balances modern urban planning with historical commemoration. The open squares, clean paths, and majestic statues complement each other, providing a rare open view in the center of Vientiane.

sisterQuote.title: A dialogue across the river
sisterQuote.text: Standing in the park, across the wide Mekong River is Nong Khai Province in Thailand. At night, the lights on both sides shine together, telling the long civilization nurtured by this great river.

food.label: Food & Drink
food.heading: Night market & street food
food.lead: As the sun sets, the famous Vientiane Night Market next to the park and countless food stalls begin to awaken.

dishes.name: Fresh juice & smoothies
dishes.desc: Fresh mango and dragon fruit smoothies, perfect for cooling down.

dishes.name: Lao BBQ skewers
dishes.desc: Charcoal-grilled meat skewers, full of aroma.

dishes.name: Papaya salad
dishes.desc: The classic Lao appetizer, spicy and refreshing.

dishes.name: Banana pancake
dishes.desc: Sweet pancakes drizzled with condensed milk, loved by tourists.

quote.text: After walking the night market, buying a snack and sitting on the riverbank steps to enjoy the breeze—this is the Vientiane night.
